title: Those who neglect the means are kept from the light by their own fault
source_text: XV. Quod si autem, inquit, alii horum dissimiles, quae praesto sunt media & auxilia neglexerint, igniculos innatos restinxerint, & veritatem, ut ait Paulus, in injustitia detinuerint, non certe aliquo fato, aut divino decreto, sed propria sua culpa ab illustriore lumine prohibentur. In jam citata Epitome Theologiae pag. 244.
pass_a_gloss: XV. But if, he says, others unlike these, have neglected the means & aids which are at hand, have quenched the innate sparks, & have held down the truth, as Paul says, in unrighteousness, not certainly by some fate, or divine decree, but by their own fault they are kept from the brighter light. In the Epitome of Theology already cited page 244.
pass_b_english: Thesis XV. 'But if others, unlike these,' he continues, 'have neglected the means and aids within their reach, put out the sparks born in them, and, as Paul says, held down the truth in unrighteousness, then it is no fate or divine decree but their own fault that shuts them out from the clearer light.'
This is in the Epitome of Theology already cited, page 244.

lemmas.latin: veritatem, ut ait Paulus, in injustitia detinuerint

they are kept from the brighter light

choices.why: The Roman school's division of grace, kept in its technical terms throughout the locus.

bible_refs: Georg Calixtus, Epitome theologiae, p. 244 (as cited in the print).
